data.content_ref: inline:§11.3 flags are sustained because of an adversarial alignment between the adjudication oracle and the artifact under test. The mechanism: the oracle that adjudicated the critics (producing SRC_007, SRC_009) and the artifact being evaluated (SRC_005) may share a common provenance or training signal. If both the oracle and SRC_005 encode the same frontier-detection heuristic, then a critic that correctly identifies a flaw in SRC_005 will necessarily disagree with the oracle's verdict and be marked failed. The §11.3 flag persists because the adjudication system cannot detect its own bias: a critic is only marked 'sound' (per SRC_006, SRC_008) when its verdict agrees with the oracle, creating a selection pressure against critics that find novel errors.
